clue.text: Socially rejected pupils in large stream

indicators.note: the pupils are placed inside the stream, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a sizeable river in Scotland and in Wales/England
a group of pupils taught together is a class

explanation.surface: A school class of outcasts finds itself in a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupils reads as schoolchildren in general but means a form taught together; the Dee is a river of Scotland and another of Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword describes someone who has fallen in social standing and is shunned by their former set.

clue.text: Liberation, in a manner, of speaking

definitions.meaning: a setting free, as in ... from captivity
the style in which a speaker uses voice and pace

explanation.surface: Freedom, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set free is a rescue from bondage, and a speaker's style of utterance is also so called.

clue.text: Daily pound a beat to uncover fraud

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char(woman)
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A newspaper pays a reporter to walk a beat exposing swindles.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning lady, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack or impostor claiming false skills is a fraud.

clue.text: Stemmed a flower

parts.note: a rose is a familiar flower

explanation.surface: A bloom had its stalk cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Stemmed reads as describing the flower, but it means came from, originated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stemmed from a cause originated or sprang up from it.

clue.text: Rescue' many imprisoned — by Friday, say

indicators.note: imprisoned places the numeral letter inside the native

parts.note: Man Friday in Robinson Crusoe was a savage, in the old term
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, standing for many

explanation.surface: Many captives are freed on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after Rescue is a print stray. Friday is Crusoe's companion, called a savage in the novel; L goes inside it after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving property from a wreck or fire is salvage.

clue.text: Ancient Greek's central part in an Olympic award

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: the central letter is set within the medal word, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a gold medal is the top Olympic award

indicators.note: the central part of a five-letter word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Greek athlete's core contribution to winning an Olympic medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of GREEK is E, which goes inside GOLD after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely old, having existed for ages, is ancient.

clue.text: Liveryman in Johnson's Club

definitions.meaning: a member of a London livery company, such as the one for workers in precious metal
Oliver, the Irish author, was a member of Samuel Johnson's literary Club

explanation.surface: A guild member belongs to Dr Johnson's Club.
explanation.walkthrough: Livery companies are ancient City of London guilds; Johnson's Club was Samuel Johnson's 18th-century literary circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman in gold would belong to that livery company, and the author of The Vicar of Wakefield joined Johnson's circle.

clue.text: College circle that is politically moderate?

parts.note: a circle is the letter O by shape
that is gives IE, and being politically moderate puts it in the centre, between R for right and L for left

explanation.surface: A college society that leans towards the centre in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: IE (that is) sits between R and L, right and left, the moderate's place.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: A faster dismissal of one would discourage

indicators.note: dismissal of works in reverse: dismissing the numeral from the answer leaves the discouraging word, so it must be inside

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A quicker sacking of a single player would dishearten.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (one) from the answer and DETER (discourage) is left. 'A faster' reads as quicker, but means someone who fasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone going without food to lose weight is fasting.

clue.text: Agree to take notes

parts.note: reads as consenting to jot things down, but the word wanted for consent is spelt only with the musical note names A to G

explanation.surface: A student agrees to write down what the lecturer says.
explanation.walkthrough: Take notes suggests jotting down a lecture; the word meaning agree is spelt wholly from musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or assent to it.

clue.text: Universally imposed back in SA. it's plain

indicators.note: back says each of the two short words is read in the opposite direction where it stands

parts.note: universally means for all
something imposed is laid on

explanation.surface: A rule applied to everyone is reversed in South Africa, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA and ON into NO. SA looks like South Africa but means South America, home of these grassy plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassland of northern South America, in Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Reason to change hands decided by East-West only?

definitions.text: Reason to change hands decided by East-West only?

parts.words: Reason to change hands decided by East-West only?
parts.note: sounds like a bridge or card game point, but means why a traveller resets the hands of a watch: the hour depends on longitude, east or west

explanation.surface: A bridge player wonders why partners swap hands only on the East-West line.
explanation.walkthrough: East-West suggests bridge partnerships; the hands are clock hands, and the time of day varies only with how far east or west you are.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour kept in a particular region depends on its longitude, so travellers reset their watches.

clue.text: De Gaulle's reversal of policy

parts.note: the French statesman stands for the French language, so the clue asks for a French phrase meaning an about-turn

explanation.surface: A French president changes his mind on policy.
explanation.walkthrough: De Gaulle's signals that the phrase wanted is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means turning the face, used for a complete about-turn in opinion or policy.

clue.text: Answer, see, found in down-to-earth part of Oxford

indicators.note: found in places the abbreviation inside the shoe part

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of lace-up shoe, and the sole is the part that touches the ground
V is the abbreviation of Latin vide, meaning see

explanation.surface: A practical-minded corner of Oxford University supplies the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university, but it is a lace-up shoe; 'found in' puts V inside its sole.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a puzzle is to find its answer, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Artist has suspicion this competition's fierce

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a suspicion can mean a trace, a tiny amount, as in a suspicion of garlic

explanation.surface: A painter is wary because the contest is so cut-throat.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspicion here is a tiny hint, like a trace, not mistrust.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the exhausting, ruthless struggle for success in modern working life.

clue.text: Alliance lamenting disorder

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the word are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A coalition breaks up amid wailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations in alignment are lined up together as allies.

clue.text: Mystery of silver mine's destruction

indicators.note: destruction of the letters breaks them up so they can be rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the word mine, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Who blew up the silver mine remains a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destruction' scrambles AG plus MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle that no one can explain is a mystery.

clue.text: Fighters for title

parts.note: sounds like boxers contending for a championship, but arms here are a coat of arms, a heraldic title, so soldiers are hinted

explanation.surface: Boxers contesting a championship belt.
explanation.walkthrough: Fighters for title suggests boxers in a title bout; the soldiers wanted are an old term for armoured troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers, especially heavily armed medieval cavalry, were so called.

clue.text: Distressed boy shortly after school broke up

indicators.note: after says the boy comes after the school

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school, and to harrow is to break up soil
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A boy gets upset just after school breaks up for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; harrowing breaks up soil, a second hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To be harrowed is to be deeply distressed or tormented.

clue.text: Roman's unmoved

parts.note: a Roman speaks Latin, so the clue asks for a Latin phrase meaning in its original place

explanation.surface: A citizen of Rome remains unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman's means in the Romans' language, Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original position, untouched.

clue.text: Area that's unstable, in disorder as result

indicators.note: in disorder means these letters are jumbled out of their order

explanation.surface: A troubled region's chaos is the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, long troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: The province of Northern Ireland saw decades of unrest, an unstable region.

clue.text: After midnight, girl and' he return to hell

indicators.note: after says the reversed names follow the middle letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G

indicators.note: return means the two words are read backwards as one run

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
he taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl and her companion come back after midnight to a terrible scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ANNE + HE into EHENNA; midnight is the middle letter of night.
explanation.definitionFit: Gehenna, the valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem, became a biblical name for the place of the damned.

clue.text: Hanging 'malevolent creature without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the creature goes around the compass point

parts.note: a goblin is a mischievous evil sprite
E for east is a compass point

explanation.surface: An evil imp hangs about with no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Without means outside here, not lacking. Hanging is a wall tapestry, from the Paris Gobelins works.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall hanging is a tapestry, and the Gobelins factory in Paris made famous ones.

clue.text: Strategic move 'from doctor in manner of running …

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the running word

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking or running
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A tactical move by a doctor, made at a run.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor; 'in' puts it inside the running word.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening in chess sacrificing material for advantage, or any calculated opening move.

clue.text: Element in old vessel heading north

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

indicators.note: heading means the first letter, the head, of north

explanation.surface: Some chemical is aboard an ancient ship sailing northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas, symbol Ar, is a chemical element.

clue.text: …hospital, say? It's just pretence

indicators.note: say means the hospital name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Guy's is a famous London teaching hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital, you say? It's only make-believe.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a well-known London hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the guise of means under a false appearance, a pretence.

clue.text: Made bus ride to word processor

indicators.note: made in the sense of made into something new, so these letters are formed into another word

explanation.surface: A commuter took the bus to the office to collect a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges BUS RIDE TO. Word processor is a witty name for someone who edits copy, not a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor's assistant processes words by correcting and cutting reporters' copy.

clue.text: This bird may fly, in a word

definitions.text: This bird may fly, in a word

parts.words: This bird may fly, in a word
parts.note: the male duck flies, and anglers give that name to the mayfly, an insect named in a single word

explanation.surface: A bird capable of flying, briefly put.
explanation.walkthrough: May fly reads as might take wing, but joined it is the mayfly, which anglers also call by the duck's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male duck has this name, and anglers apply it to a mayfly or its artificial copy.

clue.text: Union entrant successfully creates stir

parts.note: someone entering a marital union is a bride
doing something successfully is doing it well

explanation.surface: A new member of the students' union causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for prison; Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, a former London house of correction, became a general word for a jail, which slang calls stir.

clue.text: A boat-trip' round River Dart

indicators.note: round says the boat trip surrounds the river letter

parts.note: a row is an outing in a rowing boat
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Rowing a boat around the River Dart in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Dart is in Devon, but Dart is the definition; R goes after the first letter of ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart is a small pointed missile thrown or shot, like a feathered shaft.

clue.text: Double-cross representative: of. so many

parts.note: a double cross is two crosses, XX, which in Roman numerals represents a particular number

explanation.surface: A traitor acts as delegate for a large group.
explanation.walkthrough: Double-cross suggests betrayal, but it is literally two Xs: the Roman numeral for the number wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals two Xs stand for two tens, a score.

clue.text: Not experienced in prose?

definitions.meaning: lacking practice or knowledge of a subject

explanation.surface: A novice writer avoids poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpractised is inexpert, and writing free of poetic lines is literally free of verse.
